section_summary.extract_value: This section discusses the incremental contributions of 'This study' to the literature on caregiver eating messages, body image, and eating behavior. It introduces the Caregiver Eating Message Scale (CEMS), detailing its development, expert evaluation, and psychometric investigation which confirmed its two-factor structure and internal consistency over a 4-week period.
section_summary.evidence_source: General discussion This study incrementally contributes to the literature on caregiver eating messages, body image, and eating behavior by presenting the CEMS, which measures individuals' perceptions of their caregivers' tendency to restrict food intake/make critical comments about their eating and impose pressure on them to eat certain foods. Experts of various disciplines (clinical psychology, social psychology, health psychology, pediatric medicine, and dietetics) evaluated the items to ensure that they adequately and comprehensively represented the construct domain. A psychometric investigation of the CEMS indicated that it conformed to its hypothesized two-factor structure, measuring restrictive/critical caregiver eating messages and pressure to eat messages, and yielded internally consistent and stable scores over a 4-week period.

section_summary.extract_value: This section presents a general discussion of the study, focusing on the development and psychometric properties of the Caregiver Eating Messages Scale (CEMS). The CEMS measures perceptions of caregiver restriction/criticism and pressure to eat. The study found the CEMS to have a two-factor structure and internally consistent, stable scores. Figure 3 illustrates a path model testing negative body attitudes and maladaptive eating, showing path coefficients for women and men.
section_summary.evidence_source: The entire 'General discussion' section and the caption of Fig. 3.

Asset Caption.extract_value: Fig. 3. Test of the negative body attitudes and maladaptive eating model. Total scale and subscale scores serve as observed variables in the model. RCM = Restrictive Critical Messages subscale of the Caregiver Eating Messages Scale, PSPS-Family = Family subscale of the Perceived Sociocultural Pressures Scale, EDI-BD = Body Dissatisfaction subscale of the Eating Disorder Inventory-2, and EAT-26 = Eating Attitudes Test-26. Path coefficients above the path are for women; path coefficients below the path are for men. *p < .05.
